Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What would happen if Joe Biden dropped out of the presidential race?
Answer: We’re about to all find out. Because he just did.[1] This Sunday, July 21, President Joe Biden dropped out of the presidential race. In a letter to the American people he stated that it had “been an honour to serve as president” but that, “in the interests of his nation, his people and his party” he had made the painful decision to no longer seek re-election. Biden is passing on the baton. It is a brave decision. Not an entirely unexpected one — he initially declared “only an act of God” could get him to step aside. Biden then softened this stance somewhat to “a medical emergency may do the trick”… and the same day he softened his stance, he was diagnosed with Covid-19. Exhibited mild symptoms, took some rest. Continued to meet with senior members of his party. And continued to hear, time and time again, that they had lost faith in his abilities. Former President Obama, a close Biden friend and ally, recently stated he felt Biden looked incredibly disoriented at a recent fundraiser.[2] Perhaps this was the final nail in Biden’s political coffin. Then again, it was one of many. Major donors began withholding donations. Allies began speaking out, even powerful and well-connected ones. And Biden’s future in Washington began looking more and more bleak and uncertain, although doubts about Kamala Harris’ popularity remain. And now, he’s dropped out. After weeks of intense speculation. The circus is about to begin, right before what will no doubt be the craziest, most intensely followed Democratic convention in all of American history. Biden is out. Who will now take over and run against Donald Trump in his place? Time will tell — but I, for one, respect the hell out of Biden for his decision.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who is an actor or actress that you find physically unattractive but is still successful due to their acting skills?
Answer: The man himself, Steve Buscemi. He’s an awesome dude, and an amazing actor in spite of looking like some unholy cross between a reanimated bog body and Gollum. I love everything I’ve seen Mr. Buscemi in, so far. He was amazing on Boardwalk Empire. Loved him in the Sopranos. He makes even the smallest parts memorable. On top of this, he’s a firefighter as well. Was well for a long time before even making it as an actor. And during the terrorist attack on 9/11, he donned his old firefighter attire and worked on the line, right in the center of it all going down. He’s a brave man. He’s a genuinely good guy. And he’s donated millions to firefighter causes post 9/11 as well. But yeah, he’s also rather… unique looking. Those huge blue bug eyes. His expressive face a perpetual meme no matter what he says or does. I love this man, he’s easily one of the best dudes in the business. But that face! If you didn’t know he was such a chill guy, you would NOT want to run into him in a dark alley.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What leaders in history have stepped down from positions of power?
Answer: The Roman consul and general Lucius Cornelius Sulla marched into Rome, killed his enemies most brutally and installed himself as Dictator. For two years he held near-absolute power, restoring the Republic, filling the nation’s coffers with the money taken from sold off assets of his rivals, enemies and any nobleman who so much as looked at him the wrong way. He restored a sense of stability in the old Republic. He returned the powers of the senate, and took away powers from tribune of the plebs, the commoners and low folks. Sulla was thoroughly conservative. When the senate was filled to the brim with loyalists and yes-men, when all generals and all civic leaders, even religious positions, were held by those close to him, the dictator finally felt at peace. He felt untouchable. And he was. So after just two years in power, Lucius Cornelius Sulla stepped down voluntarily as dictator. He retreated to the countryside with an army of actors, prostitutes and dancers, and lived a merry drunk life full of debauchery, orgies and spending each waking hour not engaged in naughty pleasures in the writing of his memoirs. He died two years into retirement, partying himself to death.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: "Such as are thy habitual thoughts, such also will be the character of thy mind; for the soul is dyed by the thoughts." (Marcus Aurelius) What kinds of thoughts tend to dominate your mind from morning until night?
Answer: Yesterday I had a wonderful conversation with a friend of mine from Quora. We talked on Discord, a long distance call as he’s residing on the other side of the ocean. He said something that stayed with me… “I feel what we seek most, you and I, is continuity…” And that’s precisely it. Continuity. Ever since I was a kid, I hated to see my creations disturbed. The knowledge that my tower of blocks couldn’t stand forever, upset me. Why put effort into creating something beautiful if, after hours of work, it could simply be knocked over callously and hidden away in a box? Life’s kind of like that. Death knocks over all of us, every bit as callously. And like those building blocks, we end up in a box. And that’s the end of us. What I often do, is count. Count the time I already spent on this earth. And think about how much time I might have left. Notice how I use the word “might” — nothing really is given in this regard. There’s no absolute certainty that any of us will still be around tomorrow. Let alone ten, twenty of fifty years from now. Will I ever publish that great novel, will I ever build that empire, will I ever create something truly lasting in this world? And does anything really last, when even that world itself couldn’t last? That’s what I think about, most. Well that, and getting laid. Or what to cook tomorrow — good food is balm to the soul. But continuity. My legacy. How I’ll be remembered. And how I’ll look back on my life, when I’m on my deathbed. Will I be satisfied? I sure hope I won’t reach that end soon… because I’m nowhere near satisfied yet.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What's the worst thing about the current society?
Answer: An American man named Jeronimo Guerra was fixing his wife’s car in the first week of June, 2024, when it collapsed on top of him. Pinned beneath the vehicle, Guerra yelled for help… none came. Several bystanders saw he was in distress and simply went on their way. One man went to Guerra and, rather than helping him, reached into the pockets of the man’s jeans and took out his wallet, stealing it. Jeronimo’s daughter came to collect her father and found him dead and robbed. No one had come to his aid, no one had alerted authorities, and by the time she reached him, the weight of the car had crushed and killed him. Guerra was only 57. He leaved behind a son, a daughter and two young grandchildren who will now never get to know their grandfather. There’s something intensely cynical about life, when the first thing people think when they encounter a man fighting for his life isn’t the urge to save his life… but to rob him, instead. The worst thing about our society? People are heartless, and callous. They mind their own business, and only make your business theirs when there’s profit in it for them. There are still good people in this world, sure — but if you’re ever in trouble and none of those good people are around, you’d be shocked by the amount of bystanders who would simply let you perish and go on their merry way, ignoring your plight or even robbing you as you struggle for breath.
